candidates.title: MV Confiance was documented as restored for maritime museum use
candidates.summary: The National Lottery Heritage Fund recorded the Belfast Barge MV Confiance as restored for Lagan Legacy's maritime museum, with exhibition, multi-use heritage and arts space, and visitor access to maritime heritage collections.
candidates.observed_change: A former Dutch cargo barge on the River Lagan entered documented maritime museum and arts-space use after restoration.
candidates.source_date_field: Heritage Fund news date 21/01/2011 documents restored museum use; later Belfast Barge history pages describe the completed museum, arts space, and cafe fit-out.
candidates.architect: Lagan Legacy, Heritage Lottery Fund, Northern Ireland Tourist Board, Arts Council of Northern Ireland, and MV Confiance restoration project team
candidates.project_type: restored maritime heritage venue and adaptive reuse
candidates.geometry_source: Approximate point from Belfast Barge / Lanyon Quay location behind Belfast Waterfront Hall.
candidates.geometry_precision: Approximate mooring point, not a measured vessel footprint, pontoon extent, river berth, museum layout, or Lanyon Quay boundary.
candidates.limitations: The event records restored museum and arts-space use at year precision. The source does not provide a precise public-opening day; vessel condition, later fire repairs, programming, and operating status are separate evidence paths.
candidates.duplicate_check_note: Checked manual architecture milestones and tmp Belfast candidate files for MV Confiance, Belfast Barge, Lagan Legacy, Lanyon Quay, event_id variants, and source URLs; no existing manual milestone was found.
candidates.source_audit_note: The Heritage Fund page is an official funder page for the restoration; Belfast Barge venue pages corroborate location and completed venue use. This candidate stores factual metadata and URLs rather than reproducing descriptive source text.

candidates.source_date_field: Belfast Buildings Trust project page states the move to the Gate Lodge took place in January 2010.
candidates.architect: Original 1867 Good Shepherd Convent gate lodge project team; Belfast Buildings Trust reuse team not separately named on the source page
candidates.project_type: historic gate lodge reuse as heritage-trust office
candidates.geometry_source: Approximate point from 511a Ormeau Road / Gate Lodge address context.
candidates.geometry_precision: Approximate lodge point, not a measured listed-building boundary, office floor area, convent-complex boundary, or Ormeau Road frontage.
candidates.limitations: The event records institutional occupation of the Gate Lodge, not the original 1867 construction, statutory listing, full building restoration scope, or later office operations.
candidates.duplicate_check_note: Checked manual architecture milestones and tmp Belfast candidate files for Gate Lodge, Good Shepherd Convent, 511a Ormeau Road, Belfast Buildings Trust, and event_id variants; no existing manual milestone was found.

notes: Manual architecture corpus and tmp/subagents Belfast candidate files were checked by event_id, title terms, source URLs, HED references, and project names. Obvious heritage reopenings already present in the manual corpus were excluded, including Tropical Ravine, Templemore Baths, Grand Opera House, St Comgall's, Bank Buildings, City Cemetery, Titanic Hotel, St Joseph's Sailortown, SS Nomadic, HMS Caroline, and the Great Light. HED candidates are direct statutory listing-date milestones; non-HED candidates use official funder, venue, or project-owner pages and include limitations where the source gives year or month precision rather than an exact opening day.
